discussion_comments.comment_body: Addressed in 8b8cae25c. This mark was created on every `createSSEStream()` call with no clearing at all (unlike the pipeline-assembly marks in `streamingPipeline.ts`, which are cleared at the start of the next call), so it did accumulate without bound in Node's global performance timeline over a long-running server's lifetime — genuine leak. Now clears the mark immediately after creation. A wired `PerformanceObserver` still receives the entry (delivery is queued independently of the timeline buffer); `clearMarks()` only removes it from `getEntriesByName()`/`getEntriesByType()`. Left the JSON.stringify + Buffer.byteLength approach as-is (that part of the suggestion was already applied in c35e8a9b4, replacing the earlier TextEncoder allocation). New regression coverage: tests/unit/stream-request-body-size-mark-7045.test.ts.

Looked into this closely (babysit pass) and I don't think this is actually an unbounded leak, so I left this file unchanged — flagging for a human call rather than resolving.

`assembleStreamingPipeline` clears `PIPELINE_START`/`PIPELINE_END`/`PIPELINE_MEASURE` at the *start* of every call, before creating this call's marks. Since `performance.mark()` with a name that already exists always adds a new entry, that clear-before-create keeps at most one lingering set (the previous call's) at any time — bounded to O(1) per fixed name, not O(n) growth. The function itself is fully synchronous (no `await`), so two calls can't interleave and clobber each other's still-being-read marks either.

This differs from the `open-sse/utils/stream.ts` "omni-request-body-size" mark fixed in 8b8cae25c, which had *no* clearing at all and genuinely accumulated one entry per stream created — that one I fixed.

Applying the same "clear immediately after" pattern here would also break 3 existing tests in tests/unit/chatcore-streaming-pipeline.test.ts that assert the marks/measure are still readable via getEntriesByName() right after the call returns (a deliberate design choice for downstream buffer-based inspection). Happy to change it if the owner prefers immediate-clear-everywhere for consistency, but wanted to surface the tradeoff rather than silently rewrite the tests to make a non-bug go away.

Good catch — agree. Fixed in c5b912a9. The latency gate now also runs preflight when the global `defaultThresholdPercent` has been raised above the factory no-op level (2% remaining = effectively "right before 429"). Anything stricter (e.g. 20% remaining = stop at 80% used) means the operator wants enforcement and preflight runs.

Added regression test in `tests/unit/sse-auth.test.ts`: registers a fetcher, tightens the global to 20%, asserts the fetcher fires; resets to factory, asserts the fetcher does NOT fire.

Agree — fixed in 97ad78cb. Switched to a rolling buffer: chunks append onto a single `buf` and `tryScan` slices off processed bytes (`buf = buf.subarray(pos)`). No more re-concat on every `data` event, so the inner loop is O(N) instead of O(N²).

Addressed in 52345ef9.

✅ Optimized AUTO scoring by precomputing `contextTokens` and `backgroundTokens` once per `injectSkills(...)` call, then passing them into `scoreAutoSkill(...)` for each candidate.

This removes repeated token extraction in the candidate loop while keeping scoring behavior unchanged.
Good suggestion — `substring(lastIndexOf('/'))` avoids the intermediate array allocation. Applied in the next push.

Good micro-optimization suggestion. In practice this runs at most once per request (only when the direct and precomputed map lookups both miss), so the performance difference is negligible. Happy to change if preferred, but `split('/').pop()` is clearer for readability.

The `delete` operator concern is valid for hot paths. However, `translatedBody` is a per-request copy (created by `translateRequest()`), not a long-lived object. The hidden class transition affects only this one object, which is immediately serialized to JSON and sent to the provider. The alternative (`undefined` assignment) would still include the keys in `JSON.stringify()` output, potentially causing 400s from providers that reject unknown fields. Destructuring with rest/omit would be cleaner but adds complexity for 7 properties.
Agreed. Added a raw `payload.length > MAX_CURSOR_IMAGE_BYTES * 2` pre-check **before** the whitespace-strip regex so an oversized data URL can't burn CPU. Fixed in 5699daa0c.
